objective: Refine Gate 3 MeshSpec topology against the user's Spine tail reference: about 23 vertices, sparse outline and five centerline points, without overstating static or deformation quality.
inScope: Deterministic closed-contour simplification with self-intersection rejection and separate 2% foreground-loss and background-addition guards for elongated low-poly parts
Five evenly spaced cross-section centers for elongated parts instead of a uniform interior grid; a small candidate count and shape-proportional triangle area budget
Local interior-edge flips that improve the minimum angle of adjacent triangles while preserving the hull and independent topology validation
Portable curved-silhouette quality regression, updated golden MeshSpec, private real-tail comparison, 100-run determinism, and prior-Gate regression checks
outOfScope: Bones, skin weights, joint-aware edge flow, animated deformation, Spine 4.0.64 mesh serialization, and production-art approval
Changing source artwork, implicit alpha cleanup, or embedding private art in the repository
implementationSummary: The exact raster contour remains the input. For parts whose foreground bounds are at least 1.5:1 and whose raster exceeds 256 pixels, closed-arc simplification tries decreasing tolerances up to 6 raster pixels and accepts the first simple polygon with no more than 2% corrected-foreground loss or extra-background coverage. Five equally spaced major-axis cross sections select the center of the longest opaque span, giving a sparse centerline instead of a uniform grid. The other shapes retain the prior bounded 1% simplification and uniform interior sample. Earcut remains the initial triangulator; deterministic convex edge flips improve minimum angle and area splitting uses a shape-proportional budget for long parts. The independent MeshSpec validator remains unchanged. No AI computes geometry.

checks.name: Full repository verification
checks.evidence: npm run verify passed formatting, ESLint, TypeScript typecheck/build, and 5 Vitest files with 35 tests; prior Gate 0-3 tests remain passing. git diff --check passed.

checks.name: Portable curved-art quality regression
checks.evidence: A code-defined 240x320 elongated curved alpha silhouette produces a valid MeshSpec with no more than 32 total vertices and at least five interior vertices. The simplified hull has under one-third of the exact raster-outline vertices; raster foreground loss and added background each remain at or below 2%; fewer than 10% of triangles have a minimum angle under 10 degrees; a repeat run serializes identically.

checks.name: Private real-tail comparison
checks.evidence: The user's Spine screenshot visibly reports 23 vertices and shows a sparse perimeter plus centerline-oriented internal points. Read-only 294x530 Tail.png SHA-256 B62426BE390AD824DB5A691C63B9E38A61DB52405BD5AF105164C2E48BF8B7F6 uses the same explicit 0.5% alpha-cleanup budget as Gate 3: 154 detached pixels discarded, 1 corner pinch and 5 one-pixel holes filled. Baseline 1,214 vertices, 950 hull vertices, 1,476 triangles; revised mesh 24 vertices (19 hull and 5 internal), 27 triangles. On 81,641 corrected foreground pixels, the revised polygon misses 1,297 (1.589%) and covers 306 background pixels (0.375%). Zero of 27 triangles have a minimum angle below 10 degrees; maximum triangle area 5,565.625 raster pixels squared under the sparse-mode budget. Independent validator passes. The local preview was visually inspected; private source, user screenshot, and derived outputs are not committed.

checks.name: Determinism and contracts
checks.evidence: 100 additional full real-tail mesh generations of the 24-vertex result were byte-identical; the existing synthetic golden still verifies exact output after being updated for improved triangulation and repeats 100 times. MeshSpec schema, CLI contract, source alpha, and all unrelated packages are unchanged.

knownLimitations: The reference is a screenshot rather than the editable Spine mesh data, so 24 vertices and similar-looking flow do not prove vertex-for-vertex equivalence with the artist's 23-vertex mesh.

This is a static MeshSpec, not an artist-approved deformation. Gate 6 still needs root/middle/wave pose measurements and visual review after bones and weights exist; joint-aware topology may need further adjustment.

The low-poly contour does not preserve the silhouette pixel-for-pixel; its measured 1.589% foreground loss must be reviewed visually and may be unacceptable for some art even though it is under the explicit 2% bound.
The proprietary Tail.png and comparison image stay local and are not included in GitHub.

definitionOfDone.criterion: Real tail mesh approaches the supplied 23-vertex reference with centerline flow and no more than 2% raster loss or addition
Independent topology, fixed-output determinism, and all prior Gate contracts remain valid
User receives a truthful before/after image from the same private source

Do not infer exact equivalence to the screenshot or artist-approved animation.
